subject: general
question: Which enzyme is responsible for breaking down complex sugar molecules into simple glucose in humans?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amylase**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amylase** is the primary enzyme responsible for the chemical **breakdown of complex carbohydrates** (starch) into **simple sugars** such as **maltose** and **glucose**.
 
• In humans, this digestive process begins in the **mouth**, where **salivary amylase** (also known as **ptyalin**) is secreted by the **salivary glands**.
 
• The **pancreas** also produces **pancreatic amylase**, which is released into the **small intestine** to further digest any remaining starch into **monosaccharides** for absorption.
 
• **Pepsin** is an enzyme produced in the **stomach** specifically for the digestion of **proteins** into **peptides**. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Bile Juice** is produced by the **liver** and stored in the **gallbladder**; it does not contain enzymes but helps in the **emulsification of fats**. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Lipase** is an enzyme responsible for breaking down **fats (lipids)** into **fatty acids** and **glycerol**. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Carbohydrate Digestion**:

 
 
• It is a multi-step process that starts in the **oral cavity**. About **30% of starch** is hydrolyzed in the mouth by **salivary amylase** at an optimum **pH of 6.8**.
 
• The final digestion occurs in the **small intestine** where enzymes like **maltase**, **sucrase**, and **lactase** convert disaccharides into **glucose**, **fructose**, and **galactose**.
 
 
 
• **Pepsin and Protein Digestion**:
 
 
• The **stomach mucosa** contains gastric glands that secrete **proenzyme pepsinogen**.
 
• On exposure to **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl)**, pepsinogen is converted into the active enzyme **Pepsin**, which works best in an **acidic pH** of about **1.8**.
 
 
 
• **Role of Lipase**:
 
 
• **Lipases** are secreted by the **pancreas** (steapsin) and in small amounts by the **stomach** (gastric lipase).
 
• They require the presence of **bile salts** to increase the surface area of fat droplets through **emulsification**.
 
 
 
• **Bile Juice Functions**:
 
 
• **Bile** contains **bile pigments** (bilirubin and biliverdin), **bile salts**, cholesterol, and phospholipids.
 
• It neutralizes the **acidic chyme** coming from the stomach and makes the medium **alkaline** for the action of **pancreatic enzymes**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Location of Secretion**: **Salivary Amylase** is secreted in the **mouth**, while **Pancreatic Amylase** is secreted in the **duodenum**.
 
• **End Products**: The ultimate goal of **Amylase** activity is to provide the body with **Glucose**, which is the primary **energy source** for **cellular respiration**.
 
• **Enzyme Specificity**: Enzymes are highly specific; **Amylase** only acts on **alpha-1,4-glycosidic bonds** in starch and cannot digest **cellulose** due to the lack of **cellulase** in humans.
